This is pretty simple. There are a handful of ways a group of people who support some cause can incorporate. All of them are tax-exempt because they are non-profits.

If you want to start a political party, campaigning directly for a particular candidate or candidates you incorporate as a 527.

527's include a candidate's own campaign committee and various party committees which are subject to additional restrictions in how much a donor can contribute to them. But it also includes groups that are not directly associated with candidates and parties that don't have contribution limits.

If you want to start a group which doesn't campaign itself but exists to contribute directly to candidates or to political parties you incorporate as a PAC. You can only give limited amounts to each candidate.

If you just want to support a cause in general including (but not primarily!) by endorsing and campaigning for candidates you incorporate as a 501(c)(4).

If you want to support a cause but don't ever want to be involved in any electoral campaigns you can incorporate as a 501(c)(3)
